baseline.note: These are the engine's normal findings on untampered data — on-hold reserves, unsettled orders, refunds in later batches. Every detection below is counted only if it flags an entity NOT already in this set.

detection_limits.label: MDR overcharged on one transaction
detection_limits.statement: MDR overcharged on one transaction: reliably detected at or above Rs 0.09. Across 275 trials above tolerance the detection rate is 100% (95% CI 99-100%). Below the floor no claim is made, because the fault is smaller than the engine's own declared tolerance.

calibration.verdict: Underconfident: the engine is right more often than it claims (expected calibration error 0.120). This is the safe direction to be wrong in — it sends work to a human that a human did not need to do.

counterfactuals.original_reason: GST charged Rs 21.58 on a fee of Rs 179.82 is 12.00%, not the statutory 18% which would be Rs 32.37. Difference -Rs 10.79. Understated GST reduces the input tax credit the merchant can legitimately claim.

changes.text: GST would need to move by Rs 10.79 to Rs 32.37, which is 18% of the Rs 179.82 fee

counterfactual.narrative: GST here is 12.00% of the fee rather than the statutory 18%. Correcting it to Rs 32.37 clears the exception and restores Rs 10.79 of input tax credit. Understated GST is not a rounding matter — the merchant cannot claim credit that was never charged.

counterfactuals.original_reason: MDR charged Rs 184.00 on Rs 7,666.72 (2.400%) but the contracted rate for 'card' is 2.00%, which would be Rs 153.33. Overcharged by Rs 30.67.

changes.text: the fee would need to drop by Rs 30.67 to Rs 153.33
alternatively, the contracted rate for 'card' would need to be 2.400% instead of 2.00% — check whether a rate change was agreed and not reflected in the configuration

counterfactual.narrative: This clears if the fee is corrected to Rs 153.33, or if the contracted rate really is 2.400%. The two possibilities have very different consequences: a billing error is recoverable, an unrecorded rate change is not. At this transaction's frequency the difference is roughly Rs 7,667.50 a year, so it is worth resolving which it is.
